title: PV Sindhu Donates Game-Worn Jerseys to Deepika Padukone's Mental Health Foundation Sale
excerpt: Sindhu's prized jerseys and dresses go on sale from Rs 850 under the foundation's 'Closet' initiative, with proceeds funding mental health programs.
body:
• PV Sindhu has donated her game-worn jerseys and dresses to Deepika Padukone's Live Love Laugh Foundation, for sale under its 'Closet' initiative on World Mental Health Day.
  • Items are priced from Rs 850 to Rs 1,100, with proceeds funding the foundation's mental health programs.
  • The 'Closet' initiative auctions clothes from personal collections of celebrities; Deepika started it in 2019 with her own wardrobe.
  • World Mental Health Day falls on October 10 — the same day the collection went live.

Jerseys with a cause

PV Sindhu's most prized possessions are going to a good cause. The two-time Olympic medallist has donated her game-worn jerseys and dresses to Deepika Padukone's Live Love Laugh Foundation, which has put them up for sale as part of its 'Closet' initiative timed to World Mental Health Day on October 10.

"Why this pairing matters Elite athletes live under a particular kind of pressure — the loneliness of individual sport, the weight of a billion expectations, the scrutiny of every loss."

The collection is priced from Rs 850 to Rs 1,100, and every rupee goes to the foundation's mental health programs. For fans, it is a chance to own a piece of Sindhu's on-court history; for the foundation, it is a way to turn celebrity goodwill into working capital for a cause that still struggles for funding in India.

The 'Closet' initiative

Deepika Padukone founded the Live Love Laugh Foundation in 2015 after speaking publicly about her own experience with depression — a disclosure that made her one of the first major Indian public figures to talk openly about mental illness. In 2019, on World Mental Health Day, she launched the 'Closet' initiative, auctioning clothes from her personal collection with proceeds directed to the foundation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4C_wDk1mVko

The model has since expanded to other contributors, and Sindhu is among its most prominent donors yet. The badminton star and the actress have crossed paths before: in 2019, the two appeared together in a video for Prime Minister Modi's 'Bharat Ki Laxmi' initiative celebrating women's achievements.

Why this pairing matters

Elite athletes live under a particular kind of pressure — the loneliness of individual sport, the weight of a billion expectations, the scrutiny of every loss. Sindhu has spoken in the past about the mental toll of competing at the highest level. Her donation does more than raise money: it attaches one of India's most admired sporting faces to a conversation about mental health that still carries stigma, especially for young athletes and students.

For the diaspora, the resonance is double. Mental health remains an under-discussed topic in South Asian families abroad as much as at home, and seeing figures like Sindhu and Padukone normalize it gives community conversations a starting point they rarely get.

What to watch

The foundation's programs include school and rural outreach, a doctors' program, and public awareness campaigns. The question, as with any celebrity-led initiative, is scale: whether the Rs 850 jersey sales translate into sustained program funding, and whether more athletes follow Sindhu's lead in lending their names — and their closets — to the cause.
